latin.1598: XLI. Denique addit nos in primis Beatissimam Virginem laudare & honorare, pro ratione donorum quae a Deo accepit maxima. Quae, inquit, si nobiscum in terris versaretur, magno nobis honori duceremus eam cum Joanne tecto excipere, ei officia omnia exhibere, quae filii debent parentibus, cum facta sit mater fratris nostri primogeniti. Reverenter etiam cum ea colloqueremur, venerabundi salutaremus, & sanctissima ejus monita exciperemus. Sed quandoquidem in terris nobiscum non versatur, nec eam videmus, nec audimus, nec infinitam, aut ubique praesentem credere debemus, quae nunc in caelo versatur, postquam sua aetate inservisset consilio Dei, ut de Patre ipsius Davide scribitur; nos omnibus iis modis & rationibus, quibus absentes jure coli possunt & glorificari, Beatissimam Virginem reveremur & colimus, dempto religionis cultu, qui ei soli tribuitur, qui ubique praesens est, & Omnipotens, & qui scrutatur corda & renes: cujus in eo voluntati obtemperamus, quum matrem Domini Beatam & benedictam inter mulieres praedicamus: idque multis nominibus; quod credidit; quod ei factum sit juxta Verbum Angeli; quod Filium Dei enixa, eum infantem diligenter curavit & lactavit, eique optimae Matris officia omnia detulit; quod eum salvatorem suum agnovit, etiam in cunis vagientem; quod ejus verbis fidem adhibuit, contradicentibus multis; quod post sanctitatis & pietatis exquisitae in tota vita hac temporali exercitia Deo gratissima pie in Domino obdormivit, & sanctissimam animam Deo reddidit; quae in caelis fruitur ea beatitudine quam suis colentibus Deus promisit, eaque in vase illo selecto, pro ratione gratiae hic acceptae, etiam gradibus gloriae, prout Deus novit, eminente. Talem nos laudibus prosequimur, ejus memoriam gratis animis celebramus, de ea reverenter loquimur, eam virtutum exemplar Christianis omnibus, maxime piis mulieribus proponimus, omnesque ad ejus imitationem, in iis quae sunt imitanda, exhortamur. Apolog. pro sanctiss. Virg. Maria lib. 2. cap. 1.
latin.1599: XLII. His quoque consentanea tradit Joannes Dallaeus in libro de Objecto cultus religiosi. Quod enim, inquit, Angelos caeterosque beatos spiritus adorare, & precibus, aliisque religiosis honoribus colere refugimus, id non ab ullo in eos contemptu proficiscitur, sed ab unius nostri in Deum Opt. Max. officii conscientia; cui uni scilicet, preces & reliquos religionis cultus deferendos esse credimus. Salvo hoc Dei cultu, de caetero confitemur magnam esse divini in omnes caelestes spiritus operis excellentiam, Beatissimae Mariae, & sanctorum Christi Martyrum, fideliumque Ministrorum eximiam sapientiam, fidem, charitatem, sanctitatem denique atque beatitudinem: ad haec egregia in pietatis negotio facta, dicta, certamina, & saepe & libenter, quoties occurrit occasio, celebramus, & nobis, nostrisque pro sua cuique virili imitanda praedicamus: nomen postremo ac memoriam non nisi cum laude usurpamus: quae profecto omnia ostendunt Sanctos Dei & Angelos & homines, a nobis pro eo ac decet honorari, magnique fieri.
latin.1600: XLIII. Postea vero honorem, quem & Angelis & Sanctis caelo receptis nobis deferri par est, & divinorum & Ecclesiasticorum auctorum sententia, his duobus totum contineri censet, τῇ εὐφημίᾳ καὶ τῇ μιμήσει, laude & imitatione. Quorum illud prius in eo situm est, ut bene praeclareque de iis, veluti de eximiis Dei ministris, sentiamus ac loquamur: alterum vero hoc constat, ut eorum mores, & quod communi Domino ac Deo praestiterunt obsequium, fideliter ac studiose imitemur. De objecto cultus religiosi lib. 3. cap. 1.
latin.1601: XLIV. In ista autem Sanctorum Angelorum & hominum εὐφημίᾳ, sive laude, cavendum putant Scholae Reformatae Doctores, ne studio Sanctos extollendi, tribuamus ipsis titulos & elogia, quae soli Deo & Christo debentur: neve pedem inferentes in ea quae non vidimus, quicquam eis tribuamus quod per Dei verbum non constat. Cum ergo Scriptura sacra non doceat, nec indicet Sanctos in Christo defunctos rebus humanis praeesse, & viventium Patronos ac Tutores a Deo esse constitutos, nolunt illos ut tales celebrari: nec etiam iis tribui quod pro singulis fidelibus orent, & singulorum preces simul audire & exaudire possint; cum hoc nulla revelatione divina compertum sit.
latin.1602: XLV. An vero saltem in genere pro Ecclesia Militante orent quidam inter Reformatos pro certo affirmare nolunt, ac judicium suum ea de re suspendunt, ut saepe jam dictus Carolus Drelincurtius, qui censet incertum esse an Sancti pro Ecclesia orent, & istud inter occulta Dei, nec nobis revelata ponit, quia istud Scriptura nullibi clare & expresse docet. De honore B. Virgini exhibendo tom. 2. pag. 106. num. 179. & seqq.
latin.1603: XLVI. Similiter Chamierus quaestione proposita, utrum Sanctorum animae pro nobis orent in genere; hoc est universaliter pro Ecclesia Christiana, & fidelium universitate, pronunciat id nullo certo argumento constare: quamvis fateatur nonnihil habere veri similitudinis; & rem relinquat in medio, ut quisque fruatur suo judicio. Panstr. tom. 2. lib. 8. cap. 5.
latin.1604: XLVII. Alii vero non gravate concedunt, & probabile existimant Sanctos in caelis cum Christo regnantes, in genere saltem pro Ecclesia hic pugnante orare: quoniam id videtur plane consentaneum & charitati qua fervent, & communioni quae est inter utramque Ecclesiam, Militantem atque Triumphantem. Sic ea de re sententiam suam exponit Andreas Rivetus. Non negamus, inquit, Sanctorum Ecclesiam cum Christo regnantem, de membris hic pugnantibus esse sollicitam. Sed ea cura est communis, non ex cujusque conditionis notitia, sed ex generali eorum scientia, qua norunt quod, cum tota Ecclesia nondum sit recepta ubi regnant, semper aliqui militent in terra, pro quorum conservatione ac complemento, eos Deum precari, ut ejus regni incrementum semper petunt, non dubitamus. Summa controversiarum tractatu secundo, quaest. 48.
latin.1605: XLVIII. Nec alia mens est Petri Molinaei. Beati spiritus, inquit, etsi non videant quae hic fiunt, nec norint singulos, sciunt tamen Ecclesiam premi ab adversariis, & ei proposita esse perpetua certamina. Cumque ex glorificatione aucta potius sit quam imminuta eorum charitas, consentaneum est eos de Ecclesia militante esse sollicitos. In Thesauro Thesium Sedanensium Tom. 1. Thesibus de Sanctis part. 3. th. 3.
latin.1606: XLIX. Quicquid vero de eo sit, communi consensu negant Theologi Reformati Sanctos esse & recte dici Intercessores & Advocatos nostros. Quoniam intercessoris nostri apud Deum titulum solus ille meretur, qui potest omnium & singulorum preces simul & omni tempore audire atque percipere, idque habet muneris, ut illas Deo offerat & commendet. Quod uni Domino nostro Jesu Christo convenire sentiunt. Nec quisquam dixerit fideles hic degentes esse intercessores & advocatos nostros, propterea quod alii pro aliis, ex charitate mutua, orare debeamus.
latin.1607: L. Nolunt quoque bona quae nobis obtingunt Sanctorum meritis tribui, & per eorum merita quicquam a Deo postulari: quia Sancti, qui totum quod erant gratiae divinae debebant, nec sibi, nec aliis quicquam proprie loquendo, mereri potuerunt. Neque tamen propterea negant, vi communionis Sanctorum fieri, ut bona & pia opera, quae a singulis Ecclesiae membris per Dei gratiam fiunt, benedictionem & favorem Dei, in totum corpus quodammodo provocent, atque alliciant: imo quandoque Deum, hominum piorum & justorum intuitu, impiis ipsis, quibus immixti sunt, parcere, & tempus ac media poenitentiam agendi concedere: quemadmodum Dominus Abrahamo professus est se parciturum fuisse Sodomae ipsi & Gomorrhae, si in ea vel decem homines justi reperti fuissent.
latin.1608: LI. Porro ex iis quae hactenus thesibus hisce & superioribus exposita fuerunt, manifestum est nullam hic esse controversiam, An Beati tum homines, tum Angeli aliquo cultu & honore digni sint, & a nobis afficiendi: id enim ultro fatentur & docent Scholae Reformatae Doctores, nec contrarium, nisi per calumniam, ipsis imputari potest.
latin.1609: LII. Praeterea inde patet Scholae Romanae Doctores, cum Reformatis agnoscere cultum qui Sanctis hominibus & Angelis debetur, non sub eodem genere univoco cum divino cultu contineri; ac proinde non esse ejusdem cum illo speciei: nec cultum istum Religiosum esse, proprie & stricte loquendo: sed solum latiori quadam & minus propria significatione: juxta quam cultum qui Sanctis debetur religiosum dici posse expresse admittunt inter Reformatos insignes Theologi.
latin.1610: LIII. Illud quoque a nobis ostensum, Doctores Scholae Romanae fateri, distinctionem cultus Religiosi in Latriam & Duliam esse Scholae inventum; nec vocum istarum discrimen, prout in Schola Romana usurpantur, in Scriptura exacte servari: Duliam enim saepius ad cultum Deo proprium restringi, Latriam vero aliquando ad servitium humanum extendi. Vicissim autem Scholae Reformatae Doctores non multum repugnare, quin distinctionis causa, Latria divino cultui, Dulia vero observantiae illi, qua creaturae coli possunt & debent, accommodetur.
latin.1611: LIV. Tota ergo difficultas & quaestio huc redit, Qua in re consistat honor qui creaturis Sanctis & Beatis, ac praesertim Beatissimae Virgini Mariae legitime exhiberi potest? An scilicet, aedes sacrae non solum possint de nomine Sanctorum & Angelorum vocari, distinctionis causa, sed etiam eo fine condi, ut in iis Angeli & homines Sancti in caelum jam recepti publice invocentur, & variis ritibus colantur; coram iis tanquam nos intuentibus, genua flectendo, & corpus inclinando, thus iis adolendo, cereos accendendo, & donaria varia offerendo? An per eos jurare liceat, & vota illis concipere relative ad Deum, id est, quatenus Dei veritas in iis elucet, & in iis Deus per gloriam habitat? Ac denique, An illos rogare possimus ut pro nobis orent: neque hoc simpliciter, sed ad illos dirigere preces, alio quidem sensu, verum iisdem verbis & formulis conceptas, quibus sunt illae quas ad Deum concipimus? Quod affirmant Scholae Romanae Doctores & Ecclesia Romana praxi sua confirmat, negant vero communi consensu Protestantes.
latin.1612: LV. Praeterea illud in controversia est, An Sanctos in Christo defunctos celebrare liceat ut generis humani custodes & patronos, quibus rerum nostrarum regimen a Deo commissum sit: Et illos habere ut tales apud Deum Mediatores atque Intercessores, qui omni tempore omnium hominum preces sive corde, sive ore conceptas audire atque percipere, Deoque offerre & commendare possint, ac suis suffragiis ac meritis adjuvare? Praesertim vero, An Beata Virgo agnoscenda sit atque praedicanda ut Regina caeli, & mundi totius, ac creaturarum omnium Domina: ut illa per quam mundus salvatus est, & quae sola omnes haereses interemit: Et an Mater misericordiae, Mater & fons gratiae, vita & spes nostra salutari debeat: quae omnia probat praxis Ecclesiae Romanae. Improbant vero & damnant Protestantes.
latin.1613: LVI. Quibus quoque scandalum movent Elogia alia plurima, quae in Beatam Virginem & Sanctos coacervantur, a privatis quidem Doctoribus; sed Ecclesia Romana non improbante, neque prohibente: Ut quod Mariae Virgini titulus Deae tribuitur, quod Sancti Tutelaria Numina nuncupantur: ut in inscriptione illa quam ante paucos annos memini me legere, in Ecclesia apud Trecenses Beato Petro dicata, Petrus, Helena, Mastidia Tutelaria Trecensium numina. Et quod Virgini Mariae tribuitur imperium & Dominium in filium ipsum, & potestas omnia Gratiae & naturae dona sub Deo dispensandi, & quibus vult communicandi. Quod illuminatrix cordium, & rerum causa appellatur: imo dicitur mundum fundasse & fecisse, & quae in eo sunt omnia conservare & gubernare: & plura ejusmodi, quae brevitatis causa in praesens omittimus.
latin.1614: LVII. Porro Beatos Spiritus sive hominum, sive Angelorum, non esse colendos eo cultu qui ipsis in Ecclesia Romana exhibetur, dum scilicet, aedes sacrae & altaria in eorum honorem construuntur atque dedicantur, cerei illis accenduntur, incensum adoletur, & coram ipsis tanquam intuentibus genua flectuntur: dum vota eis nuncupantur, & variae fiunt illis oblationes, ac juramenta per eorum nomen concipiuntur: dum denique precibus solennibus ad eorum auxilium & opem confugitur, & hymni illis publice canuntur in gratiarum actionem pro beneficiis a Deo acceptis, & si qua sunt hujusmodi: nec Angelos, inquam, beatos, nec Sanctos in Christo defunctos eo modo colendos esse, inde probant primum Protestantes, quod talis cultus non debuit ab hominibus sine Dei verbo excogitari. Alioqui sine fide exhibebitur: cum absque Dei verbo nemo certus esse possit illum Deo gratum & acceptum esse. Adeoque si constet ejusmodi cultum nullo Dei praecepto & revelatione niti, inter ἐθελοθρησκείας ab Apostolo damnatas merito rejici potest. Jam vero totum illum cultum in Dei verbo nullum fundamentum habere, ex eo patet, quod in universa Scriptura seu Veteris, seu Novi Testamenti, nullum ejus extat praeceptum, aut exemplum.
latin.1615: LVIII. Et quidem quod ad Vetus Testamentum attinet, fatentur ipsi Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae cultum qui Sanctis defunctis apud ipsos exhiberi solet in Ecclesia Veteris Testamenti usitatum non fuisse. Cujus rei hanc rationem afferunt, quod animae Sanctorum tum temporis nondum fruebantur illa caelesti gloria & beatitudine, ad quam post Christi adventum evectae sunt: sed in quodam veluti carcere detinebantur, quem carcerem limbum Patrum vocant. At saltem nulla ratio est cur cultus quem Angelis exhibent, si quidem legitimus sit, sub Veteri Testamento non debuerit Angelis exhiberi. Imo si unquam colendi sunt Angeli, tum maxime coli debuerunt: cum in populo veteri gubernando Angelorum ministerio Deus plerunque sit usus, & frequentes fuerint in Ecclesia Judaica illorum apparitiones: quia scilicet, Deus illis internunciis apud fideles saepius utebatur. Cum in Ecclesia Novi Testamenti locutus sit nobis Deus per Filium, cui & non Angelis mundum hunc futurum subjecit, ut docet Apostolus Heb. 2. 3. Et tamen neque ex Scriptura sacra, nec etiam ex ullis historiae & Gentis Judaicae monumentis, ostendi potest vel minimam cultus publici partem Angelis impensam fuisse, exempli causa, in honorem eorum ullum sacellum vel oratorium fuisse consecratum, ullave festa celebrata, & vel unicum cereum, aut thuris granum illis oblatum & accensum fuisse: aut in publicis fidelium coetibus ullas fuisse ad ipsos preces conceptas, & hymnos decantatos, vel ullam denique adorationis speciem exhibitam. Quin contrarium plane apud omnes indubie constat. Cum tamen nihil prohiberet, imo maxime conveniret Angelos tali cultu apud Judaeos prosequi, si quidem istud apud nos liceret.
latin.1616: LIX. Sub Novo vero Testamento Christus & Apostoli hac in parte nihil omnino immutarunt. Nec ullum novum cultum instituerunt, quo deinceps Angeli & Justorum Spiritus ad videndam Dei faciem admissi colerentur. Etenim hujus rei nullum praeceptum, aut exemplum, vel etiam minimum indicium apparet in tota Novi Testamenti Scriptura. In qua nullibi monemur Angelos aut Sanctos defunctos invocare, ad eorum opem confugere, hymnos illis publice canere, eosque thure, incenso, altaribus & aedibus sacris, aut quibuslibet aliis externis adorationis actibus honorare.
latin.1617: LX. Neque solum altum est de rebus istis silentium in scriptis Novi Testamenti, sed nec ex Ecclesiastica trium primorum saeculorum traditione simile quid exsculpi potest. Non pauci fuerunt illustres per istud tempus apud Christianos scriptores, quorum monumenta supersunt, & qui in manibus hominum versantur. Quales apud Latinos Tertullianus, Cyprianus, Lactantius, & Arnobius; & apud Graecos Justinus, Athenagoras, Irenaeus, Clemens Alexandrinus, Origenes & alii complures: apud quos nullibi legitur cultum aliquem hodierno in Ecclesia Romana similem, Angelis & Sanctis mortuis, vel exhibitum olim, vel jam exhibendum esse: contrarium vero multis & manifestis admodum indiciis colligitur.
latin.1618: LXI. Primo enim, qui secundo & tertio post Christum saeculo vixerunt scriptores Ecclesiastici, in ea plerique fuerunt sententia, omnium fidelium, etiam sanctissimorum, animas certis extra caelum locis, ad supremum judicii diem contineri, neque ante receptum ex resurrectione corpus in patriam illam caelestem admitti. Eorum quidem nonnulli, ex singulari quadam praerogativa, specialem locum Martyribus assignant, paradisum scilicet, ut vocant. Sed eo nomine minime designant caelum ipsum summum, in quo Martyres Dominum videant facie ad faciem: verum regionem quandam subcaelestem, sinu quidem Abrahae, in quo reliquorum piorum animae requiescunt, laetiorem & amoeniorem, non tamen caelestis gloriae capacem: ut adversus Cardinales Bellarminum atque Perronium, fuse demonstrat inclytae memoriae Joannes Dallaeus. Unde patet primis illis Christianismi saeculis, nondum ut traditionem Apostolicam receptum fuisse dogma de illo Sanctorum cultu & invocatione, qui in Ecclesia Romana jam obtinet. Etenim cultus ille nititur hypothesi de Sanctorum gloria & Beatitudine summa. Ad quam cum non admitterentur, juxta Scholam Romanam, Sanctorum animae ante Christi adventum, ideo fatentur illos nondum fuisse solenniter cultos & invocatos. De poenis & satisfactionibus lib. 5. cap. 3. 4. 5. & 6. Et De Objecto cultus Religiosi lib. 3. cap. 22.
latin.1619: LXII. Deinde ex vetustissimis quae supersunt Liturgiis constat, veteres illos Christianos obtulisse Deo preces & supplicationes pro omnibus omnino mortuis, etiam pro Sanctissimis, pro Martyribus, pro Apostolis, adeoque pro ipsa Deipara Virgine. Pro quibus a Deo petunt in Liturgiis illis ut eos requiescere faciat in regione viventium, & largiatur iis promissionum suarum bona, & praestet requiem bonamque memoriam: non vero, simpliciter, ut frustra contendit Bellarminus, pro iis gratiarum actiones offerunt. Jam vero ex quo publice receptus est Religiosus Sanctorum cultus & invocatio, tanquam oraculum illud Augustini habitum est, Injuriam facere Martyri qui orat pro Martyre. Nec unquam aliquis in animum inducet ut utatur solenni illa invocatione, quam Sanctis cum Christo regnantibus deberi docet Ecclesia Romana, apud eos quos opus sit precibus nostris Deo commendari.
latin.1620: LXIII. Praeterea cum Gentium sapientes unum tantum summum Deum agnoscere se profiterentur, alios vero quos Deos vocabant unici illius summi numinis esse Ministros, & secundo solum post eum loco coli: ac Christianis objicerent quod supremi illius Dei cultu contenti, negligerent inferiores sub illo potestates, quibus tamen sua quoque veneratio debetur: veteres illi Christiani bona fide agnoverunt se revera tantum unum summum Deum colere, idque tanquam legitimum & rectum defenderunt; nec vel minimam cultus religiosi partem ipsis bonis & Sanctis Dei Ministris debitam esse concesserunt, aut cultum Religiosum in summum & subalternum, vel absolutum atque relativum distinxerunt: Quod tamen ab ipsis postulabat candor, charitas, atque prudentia, si de Sanctorum & Angelorum cultu idem cum hodierna Ecclesia Romana sensissent.
latin.1621: LXIV. Nam ad istam Ethnicorum criminationem sic cum Arnobio respondent. Ad cultum divinitatis obeundum satis est nobis Deus primus, pater rerum ac Dominus, constitutor, moderatorque cunctorum. In hoc omne quod colendum est colimus, quod adorare convenit adoramus, quod obsequium venerationis exposcit, venerationibus promeremur. Cum enim divinitatis ipsius teneamus caput, a quo ipsa divinitas divinorum omnium, quaecunque sunt, ducitur, supervacuum putamus personas ire per singulas, cum & ipsi qui sint, & quae habeant nomina nesciamus, & cujus sint praeterea numeri, neque liquidum, neque comprehensum, neque exploratum habere possimus. Quod postea illustrat illa ipsa ab aulis principum allata similitudine quam eadem hac in re Ethnici usurpabant. Atque, inquit, ut in terrestribus regnis necessitate nulla compellimur, regalibus in familiis constitutos nominatim cum principibus adorare, sed in Regum ipsorum cultu quicquid illis annexum est tacita vi se sentit honorificentia comprehendi; non alia ratione quicunque hi dii sunt, quos esse nobis proponitis, si sunt progenies regia, & principali oriuntur e capite, etiamsi nullos accipiant a nobis nominatim cultus, intelligunt se tamen honorari communiter cum suo Rege, atque in illius venerationibus contineri. Arnob. contra gentes lib. 3. init.
latin.1622: LXV. Quibus congruunt quae docet Origenes simile tractans argumentum. Nam Celso contendenti nunquam quidem a Dei cultu deficiendum esse & animam in illum intentam esse debere in omni opere & cogitatione, verum id non obstare quominus placandae propitiandaeque sint variae potestates sub Deo constitutae, idque ad summi numinis honorem redundare, Respondet insignis ille veteris Ecclesiae Doctor, Ad hoc ut Angeli Dei nobis propitii sint, & pro nobis omnia faciant, sufficit & noster primo in Deum affectus, nostraque dispositio, quantum quidem humana natura valet, imitans ipsorum Angelorum Deum imitantium judicium, & secundo Filii Dei verbique pro nostra virili apprehensio. Item, Unus nobis est placandus Deus universorum Dominus, & hunc ut propitium habeamus, orandum est, qui pietate & omni virtute propitiatur. Sin & post hunc supra omnes Deum aliquos alios propitios velit, cogitet quod sicut moto corpore umbra quoque ipsius movetur; ita cum aliquis summum Deum habet propitium, sequitur ut propitios habeat omnes ejus amicos, Angelos, animas, spiritus; sentiunt enim qui sint favore Dei digni, quibus non ipsi solum bene volunt; verum etiam cum iis, qui Deum colere volunt, operam jungunt, eumque placant, & una nobiscum precantur & postulant; ita ut audeamus dicere hominibus, qui cum firmo animi proposito meliora eligunt, ac sequuntur, quoties ii Deum precantur, innumerabiles potestates sacras una cum iis non vocatas precari, fragili ac mortali nostro generi se una socias praebentes, ac ut sic dicam concertantes, & nobis in hoc agone collaborantes. Contra Celsum lib. 5. Contra eundem Celsum lib. 8.
latin.1623: LXVI. Ubi valde notandum est quod dicit Origenes, innumerabiles potestates sacras, quo nomine Angelos & Spiritus Beatos designat, una cum iis qui Deum colere volunt, precari quidem, sed ἀκλήτους, non vocatas. Nec enim solum in genere docet unum Deum esse adorandum, & religiose colendum indivisibiliter & inseparabiliter, sed etiam preces nostras ad eum solum dirigendas esse, nec ulla precationis & invocationis specie erga Beatos Angelos, aut alias quascunque creaturas utendum. Apage, inquit, hoc Celsi consilium jubentis orari daemonas (id est, Spiritus qui summo Deo ministrant, ex Platonicorum more atque loquendi usu) qui ne tantillum quidem audiendus est. Soli enim Deo Optimo Maximo preces offerendae sunt; Et vero unigenito Dei verbo, primogenito creaturae totius offerendae, qui ut Pontifex rogandus est, ut nostram, quae ad eum pervenit, orationem perferat ad Deum suum & Deum nostrum, Patrem suum, & Patrem nostrum. Eodem contra Celsum lib. 8. Ejusdem vero operis libro quinto, Omnem, inquit, precationem, atque orationem, omnem obsecrationem, & gratiarum actionem Deo summo rerum omnium Domino, per vivum verbum, Deumque, Pontificem qui supra omnes Angelos est, emittere, seu deferre decet. Ipsum autem etiam verbum orabimus, & interpellabimus, & gratias ei agemus, precesque etiam offeremus, si modo intelligere possimus propriam & Catachrestice dictam precandi rationem. Angelos enim a nobis, qui eorum scientiam, sive notitiam, rem scilicet supra homines constitutam minime accepimus, invocari, a ratione alienum est. Et ut demus, eorum notitiam, quae mirabilis & arcana est, comprehendi, haec ipsa notitia eorum naturam, & quibus, vel ad quae singuli praefecti atque ordinati sint demonstrans, prohibebit ne audeamus ullum alium precari, quam Dominum qui est supra omnia, quique abunde ad omnia sufficit, per servatorem nostrum Dei filium.
latin.1624: LXVII. Hic etiam observandum est Origenem, ut multos alios illius aevi Scholae Christianae Doctores, existimasse Solem, Lunam, & reliqua Sydera esse animantia quaedam rationalia, & virtute praedita, & cognitionis lumine illustrata a sapientia illa quae est splendor aeterni luminis: nec eum ullo modo repugnare Celso illos praedicanti, tanquam illustrissimos rerum superiorum praecones, ac vere caelestes Angelos, ipsique plene persuasum fuisse, quod Sol, Luna, & Stellae preces Deo offerrent rerum omnium Domino per unigenitum ejus. Proinde si aliquo religionis cultu, ex Origenis mente, digni sint Angeli Dei, eo quoque par est dignum existimari Solem, Lunam, & Astra. Et tamen querente Celso quod Judaei Solem, Lunam, & Planetas non colant, non solum in genere negat fas esse creaturas illas σέβειν καὶ προσκυνεῖν, colere atque adorare; sed etiam asserit illicitum esse illis supplicare, & hymnos canere. Judicamus, inquit, non decere eos precari qui ipsi precantur. Quin addit Solem & sydera ipsa ita velle, nosque ad Deum, quem ipsa precantur, remittere potius quam ad seipsa dejicere ac demittere, vel eam quam habemus precandi potestatem a Deo dividere, & aliquam ejus partem etiam sibiipsis sumere. Et postea subjungit, Cum Dominus ubique nobiscum & prope nos adsit, absurdum esse quaerere eum precari, qui non ad omnia usque pertingit, Solem, & Lunam, vel aliam aliquam Stellam. Ac denique Celso scribenti eo nos magnum Deum magis colere videri, si & Soli hymnos canamus, Respondet se contrarium scire. Hymnos enim, inquit, in solum Deum universorum Dominum dicimus, & in unigenitum ejus Deum verbum. Adversus Celsum lib. 5.
latin.1625: LXVIII. Neque est quod quis dicat cum Cardinali Perronio, quum negat Origenes Angelos precandos & invocandos esse, illum agere de Oratione quam absolutam vocant, non vero de ea quae Relativa dicitur, qua sola apud Angelos utendum esse docet Schola Romana. Etenim Celsus ipse, adversus quem agit Origenes, non existimabat Angelos, sive ut loquitur cum Platone, daemonas colendos esse cultu summo & absoluto, sed eo qui ad Deum summum, cujus ministri essent, referretur. Adeoque contra Christianos invocandos illos esse contendebat non absoluta quadam precatione, quasi primi & summi essent bonorum largitores, sed relativa solum, ut eorum sub Deo summo impetratores & administratores. Ac proinde cum Origenes neget illos invocandos esse, qua ratione Celsus, & alii sapientes Ethnicorum volebant, planum est, juxta Origenem, nec absoluta, neque relativa invocatione licitum esse apud illos uti. Adde quod Origenes dicens illos pro nobis precari ἀκλήτους, non vocatos, satis indicat illos nequidem rogandos esse ut Deum pro nobis precentur: quod est precationem relativam illis denegare, non vero tantum absolutam.
latin.1626: LXIX. Itaque Origenes pulsatus Celsi objectionibus, quasi Christiani summi Dei Ministros, & Angelicas potestates contemnerent, & nullo honore prosequerentur, non alium honorem illis exhibendum esse concedit, quam eum qui consistit in laude & imitatione: Eos, inquit, praedicamus beatos, & bene loquimur de illis, quibus a Deo commissae sunt utilitates hominum, non tamen honorem Deo debitum his reddimus. Saepius jam citato libro adversus Celsum Philosophum octavo. Ac praeterea loco quem supra descripsimus ex libro quinto ejusdem operis, affirmat Angelos, quantum humana natura fert, nobis imitandos esse; idque satis fore ut beati illi Spiritus bene nobis velint, & pro nobis in omnibus satagant: sed nullibi, quod tamen ad ejus scopum maxime fecisset, & calumniam Ethnicorum plenius adhuc retudisset, memorat nos eorum orationes precibus ambire, aut quicquam eorum quae in Ecclesia Romana hodie usitata sunt, in eorum honorem fieri.
latin.1627: LXX. Proinde quum Origenes octavo illo adversus Celsum libro, insinuat quandam θεραπείαν, id est, honoris & observantiae speciem veris Dei Ministris, Gabrieli, Michaeli, caeterisque Angelis & Archangelis deberi, θεραπεία ista, juxta doctrinam Origenis, nullo modo constitui potest in quadam eorum adoratione, & invocatione, quae in solidum & indivisibiliter uni summo Deo deberi contendit: sed in illa beatitudinis, gloriae & sanctitatis agnitione & celebratione, & etiam obsequii & amoris erga Deum pia imitatione, quibus Sanctos Angelos colere nos posse fatetur.

sections.title: Rivet on the Virgin: every honor fit for the absent, short of religious worship
sections.pass_a: Finally he adds that we above all praise and honor the most Blessed Virgin, according to the measure of the very great gifts which she received from God. She, he says, if she were living with us on earth, we would count it a great honor to us to receive her under our roof with John, to show her all the duties which children owe to parents, since she was made the mother of our firstborn brother. We would also speak with her reverently, greet her with veneration, and receive her most holy counsels. But since she does not live with us on earth, and we neither see her nor hear her, nor ought we to believe her infinite or everywhere present, she who now lives in heaven after she had served the counsel of God in her own generation, as is written of her father David; we revere and honor the most Blessed Virgin in all those ways and manners in which absent persons can rightly be honored and glorified, religious worship being taken away, which is given to him alone who is everywhere present, and Almighty, and who searches hearts and reins: whose will we obey in this when we proclaim the mother of the Lord blessed and blessed among women: and this on many grounds; that she believed; that it was done to her according to the Word of the Angel; that having borne the Son of God she diligently cared for him as an infant and nursed him, and rendered him all the duties of the best Mother; that she acknowledged him as her saviour, even crying in the cradle; that she gave faith to his words, while many contradicted; that after exercises of holiness and exquisite piety most pleasing to God through the whole of this temporal life she fell asleep piously in the Lord, and gave back her most holy soul to God; who in heaven enjoys that blessedness which God promised to those who worship him, that blessedness in that chosen vessel also excelling in degrees of glory, according to the measure of grace received here, as God knows. Such a one we follow with praises, we celebrate her memory with grateful minds, we speak of her reverently, we set her forth as a pattern of virtues to all Christians, especially to pious women, and we exhort all to imitate her, in those things which are to be imitated. Apology for the most holy Virgin Mary, book 2, chapter 1.
pass_b: Rivet ends by saying that we honor the most Blessed Virgin first of all, in proportion to the very great gifts God gave her.

"If she were living among us on earth," he writes, "we would think it a great honor to take her into our home as John did and to give her every duty that children owe their parents, since she became the mother of our firstborn brother. We would speak to her with reverence, greet her with veneration, and take her most holy counsel to heart."

"But she is not living among us on earth. We neither see nor hear her, and we must not believe that she is infinite or present everywhere. She is now in heaven, having served God's purpose in her own generation, as Scripture says of her father David. So we revere and honor the most Blessed Virgin in every way that the absent can rightly be honored and glorified, except religious worship, which belongs to him alone who is present everywhere, who is almighty, and who searches hearts and minds."

"In this we obey his will when we call the Lord's mother blessed, blessed among women, and for many reasons: she believed; it was done to her as the angel had said; after bearing the Son of God she cared for him and nursed him as a baby and gave him every service of the best of mothers; she acknowledged him as her Savior even when he was crying in the cradle; she trusted his words when many spoke against him; and after a whole earthly life spent in exercises of holiness and rare piety, most pleasing to God, she fell asleep devoutly in the Lord and gave back her most holy soul to God."

"In heaven she enjoys the blessedness God promised to those who worship him, and in that chosen vessel it stands out, as God knows, even in degrees of glory, in proportion to the grace she received here. We praise such a woman, keep her memory with grateful hearts, and speak of her with reverence. We hold her up to all Christians, and above all to devout women, as a model of the virtues, and we urge everyone to imitate her in whatever is to be imitated." (Apology for the Most Holy Virgin Mary, book 2, chapter 1.)

choices.why: The ablative absolute marks the one honor withheld from Mary while all honors due the absent are granted.

sections.title: Daillé: refusing prayer to angels is not contempt but loyalty to God alone
sections.pass_a: With these things John Daillé also teaches consonant things in the book On the Object of Religious Worship. For that, he says, we shrink from adoring the Angels and the other blessed spirits, and from honoring them with prayers and other religious honors, that does not proceed from any contempt toward them, but from the consciousness of our duty toward the one God, Best and Greatest; to whom alone, namely, we believe prayers and the remaining worships of religion are to be rendered. This worship of God being kept safe, for the rest we confess that great is the excellence of the divine work in all the heavenly spirits, the exceptional wisdom, faith, charity, holiness and finally blessedness of the most Blessed Mary, and of the holy Martyrs of Christ, and of his faithful Ministers: moreover their outstanding deeds, sayings, contests in the business of piety, we celebrate both often and gladly, whenever occasion occurs, and we proclaim them to be imitated by ourselves and our people, each according to his strength: finally we use their name and memory only with praise: all of which things surely show that the Saints of God, both Angels and men, are honored by us as is fitting, and are highly esteemed.
pass_b: John Daillé teaches the same in his book On the Object of Religious Worship.

"When we decline to adore the angels and the other blessed spirits, or to honor them with prayers and other religious honors," he writes, "this does not come from any contempt for them. It comes from our conscience about the duty we owe to the one God, best and greatest, to whom alone, we believe, prayers and the other acts of religious worship are to be offered."

"With this worship of God kept intact, we gladly confess the rest: the excellence of God's work in all the heavenly spirits is great, and great too are the wisdom, faith, love, holiness, and, finally, the blessedness of the most Blessed Mary, of Christ's holy martyrs, and of his faithful ministers. We celebrate their outstanding deeds, words, and struggles in the cause of godliness often and gladly, whenever there is occasion, and we commend them to ourselves and our people for imitation, each as far as he is able. And we never speak their name or memory except with praise. All of this shows that God's saints, angels and men alike, are honored by us as is fitting and held in high esteem."

lemmas.gloss: this worship of God being kept safe
each according to his own strength

choices.why: Daillé presents the refusal as a reverent scruple, not as hostility; 'decline' keeps the restraint.

sections.title: Daillé: honor of the saints consists in praise and imitation
sections.pass_a: But afterwards he judges that the honor which it is fitting for us to render both to Angels and to Saints received into heaven, by the judgment both of the divine and the Ecclesiastical authors, is wholly contained in these two, in eulogy and in imitation, praise and imitation. Of which the former is placed in this, that we think and speak well and nobly of them, as of excellent ministers of God: but the other consists in this, that we faithfully and zealously imitate their manners, and the obedience which they rendered to the common Lord and God. On the Object of Religious Worship, book 3, chapter 1.
pass_b: Daillé then holds that the honor we rightly give to the angels and to the saints received into heaven is, by the judgment of both the inspired and the church writers, entirely contained in two things: in good report and in imitation, that is, praise and imitation.

The first means thinking and speaking well and highly of them as outstanding servants of God. The second means imitating faithfully and earnestly their way of life and the obedience they gave to their Lord and God, who is ours as well. (On the Object of Religious Worship, book 3, chapter 1.)

lemmas.gloss: of the divine (biblical) and Ecclesiastical authors

choices.why: Daillé distinguishes biblical from church authors; 'inspired' makes the contrast plain in English.

sections.title: Cautions in praising the saints: no divine titles, no unrevealed patronage or hearing of prayers
sections.pass_a: But in that eulogy, or praise, of the Saints, Angels and men, the Doctors of the Reformed School think care must be taken lest, from zeal of extolling the Saints, we attribute to them titles and eulogies which are owed to God and Christ alone: or lest, setting foot into things which we have not seen, we attribute to them anything which is not established through the word of God. Since therefore sacred Scripture does not teach, nor indicate, that the Saints who died in Christ preside over human affairs, and have been appointed by God Patrons and Guardians of the living, they will not have them celebrated as such: nor also that it be attributed to them that they pray for individual believers, and can at once hear and grant the prayers of individuals; since this has been found out by no divine revelation.
pass_b: In this good report or praise of the saints, angels and men, the teachers of the Reformed school think we must take care not to give them, in our eagerness to exalt them, titles and tributes owed to God and Christ alone. Nor should we intrude into things we have not seen and credit them with anything that the word of God does not establish.

Holy Scripture neither teaches nor hints that the saints who have died in Christ govern human affairs or have been appointed by God as patrons and guardians of the living. So the Reformed refuse to celebrate them in that role. Nor will they credit the saints with praying for individual believers, or with being able to hear and answer the prayers of many people at once, since no divine revelation has disclosed this.

lemmas.latin: pedem inferentes in ea quae non vidimus
lemmas.gloss: setting foot into things we have not seen
to hear and to grant (hear favorably)

choices.term: pedem inferentes in ea quae non vidimus
choices.english: intrude into things we have not seen
choices.why: An echo of Colossians 2:18; 'intrude' keeps the note of overreach.

sections.title: Whether the saints pray for the Church in general: Drelincourt suspends judgment
sections.pass_a: But whether at least in general they pray for the Militant Church, some among the Reformed are unwilling to affirm for certain, and suspend their judgment on that matter, as the often already mentioned Charles Drelincourt, who judges it to be uncertain whether the Saints pray for the Church, and places this among the hidden things of God, not revealed to us, because Scripture nowhere teaches this clearly and expressly. On the honor to be shown to the Blessed Virgin, volume 2, page 106, number 179 and following.
pass_b: Whether the saints at least pray for the Church Militant in general, some among the Reformed will not affirm as certain and suspend judgment on the question.

One is Charles Drelincourt, cited often already, who judges it uncertain whether the saints pray for the Church. He places this among God's hidden things, not revealed to us, because Scripture nowhere teaches it clearly and expressly. (On the Honor to Be Shown to the Blessed Virgin, volume 2, page 106, number 179 and following.)

lemmas.gloss: among the hidden things of God

choices.term: inter occulta Dei, nec nobis revelata
choices.english: among God's hidden things, not revealed to us
choices.why: Echoes Deuteronomy 29:29, the Reformed ground for suspending judgment.

sections.title: Chamier: the general prayer of saints is likely but not proven
sections.pass_a: Similarly Chamier, the question being proposed, whether the souls of the Saints pray for us in general; that is universally for the Christian Church, and the whole body of the faithful, pronounces that this is established by no certain argument: although he admits that it has something of likelihood; and he leaves the matter in the middle, so that each may enjoy his own judgment. Panstratia, volume 2, book 8, chapter 5.
pass_b: Chamier likewise takes up the question whether the souls of the saints pray for us in general, that is, for the Christian Church as a whole and for the whole body of believers. He declares that no certain argument establishes it, though he grants it has some likelihood, and he leaves the matter open for each to decide for himself. (Panstratia, volume 2, book 8, chapter 5.)

lemmas.gloss: leaves the matter in the middle

choices.why: An idiom for undecided questions; 'open' conveys it without a literal 'in the middle'.

sections.title: Rivet: the reigning saints pray in general for the Church still fighting
sections.pass_a: But others concede without reluctance, and judge it probable, that the Saints reigning with Christ in heaven pray at least in general for the Church fighting here: since that seems plainly consonant both with the charity with which they burn, and with the communion which is between both Churches, the Militant and the Triumphant. So Andrew Rivet sets out his opinion on that matter. We do not deny, he says, that the Church of the Saints reigning with Christ is anxious about the members fighting here. But that care is common, not from the knowledge of each one's condition, but from their general knowledge, by which they know that, since the whole Church has not yet been received where they reign, some always fight on earth, for whose preservation and completion we do not doubt that they pray to God, as they always ask for the increase of his kingdom. Summary of Controversies, second treatise, question 48.
pass_b: Others readily grant, and think it probable, that the saints reigning with Christ in heaven pray at least in general for the Church fighting here, since this seems wholly in keeping with the love that burns in them and with the communion between the two Churches, the Church Militant and the Church Triumphant.

Andrew Rivet states his view this way: "We do not deny that the Church of the saints who reign with Christ cares for the members still fighting here. But that care is general. It does not come from knowing each person's condition but from their general knowledge: they know that the whole Church has not yet been received where they reign, and that some are always fighting on earth. We do not doubt that they pray to God for the preservation and completion of these, just as they always ask for the growth of his kingdom." (Summary of Controversies, second treatise, question 48.)

choices.why: Rivet contrasts a care for the whole Church with knowledge of individual cases; 'general' carries that contrast.

sections.title: Du Moulin: the blessed know the Church is pressed, and so are concerned for it
sections.pass_a: Nor is the mind of Peter du Moulin otherwise. The blessed spirits, he says, although they do not see the things that happen here, nor know individuals, nevertheless know that the Church is pressed by adversaries, and that perpetual contests are set before it. And since from glorification their charity has been increased rather than diminished, it is consonant that they are anxious about the militant Church. In the Treasury of Sedan Theses, volume 1, in the Theses on the Saints, part 3, thesis 3.
pass_b: Peter du Moulin is of the same mind. "The blessed spirits," he says, "do not see what happens here and do not know individuals, yet they know that the Church is hard pressed by its enemies and faces endless struggles. Since glorification has increased their love rather than lessened it, it is fitting that they should be concerned for the Church Militant." (Treasury of Sedan Theses, volume 1, Theses on the Saints, part 3, thesis 3.)

lemmas.latin: ex glorificatione aucta potius quam imminuta
lemmas.gloss: increased rather than diminished by glorification

choices.why: Du Moulin claims general solicitude, not active intercession for individuals; 'concerned' keeps that limit.

sections.title: The saints are not our intercessors and advocates: that title is Christ's alone
sections.pass_a: But whatever may be of that, by common consent the Reformed Theologians deny that the Saints are and are rightly called our Intercessors and Advocates. Because he alone merits the title of our intercessor with God, who can hear and perceive the prayers of all and of each at once and at every time, and has this as his office, that he offers them to God and commends them. Which they judge belongs to our one Lord Jesus Christ. Nor would anyone say that the faithful living here are our intercessors and advocates, on the ground that we ought to pray, some for others, out of mutual charity.
pass_b: However that may be, the Reformed theologians agree in denying that the saints are, or can rightly be called, our intercessors and advocates.

Only he deserves the title of our intercessor with God who can hear and take in the prayers of all people and of each one, at once and at all times, and whose office it is to offer and commend them to God. That, they hold, fits our Lord Jesus Christ alone. Nor would anyone call the believers living here our intercessors and advocates merely because, out of mutual love, we ought to pray for one another.

lemmas.gloss: and has this as his office

choices.why: The term echoes 1 John 2:1, where Christ is the Advocate with the Father.

sections.title: No merits of the saints, yet the godly may draw God's favor on the whole body
sections.pass_a: They also will not have the good things which befall us attributed to the merits of the Saints, and anything requested from God through their merits: because the Saints, who owed the whole of what they were to divine grace, could merit nothing, properly speaking, either for themselves or for others. Nor yet on that account do they deny that it happens by force of the communion of the Saints, that the good and pious works which are done by individual members of the Church through the grace of God, in some way call forth and attract the blessing and favor of God upon the whole body: indeed that sometimes God, in regard to pious and just men, spares the impious themselves, with whom they are mixed, and grants time and means of doing penitence: just as the Lord professed to Abraham that he would have spared Sodom itself and Gomorrah, if even ten just men had been found in it.
pass_b: The Reformed also refuse to credit the good things that come to us to the merits of the saints, or to ask anything of God through their merits. The saints owed all that they were to divine grace, and so, strictly speaking, they could merit nothing either for themselves or for others.

Yet they do not therefore deny that, by virtue of the communion of saints, the good and godly works that individual members of the Church do by God's grace in some way call down and draw God's blessing and favor on the whole body. Indeed, God sometimes spares the ungodly themselves for the sake of the godly and righteous who live among them, and gives them time and means to repent, just as the Lord declared to Abraham that he would have spared Sodom and Gomorrah if even ten righteous people had been found there.

lemmas.gloss: by force of the communion of the Saints

choices.why: God's regard for the righteous is a reason for sparing, not a merit paid; 'for the sake of' keeps that sense.

sections.title: No controversy over whether the blessed deserve some honor
sections.pass_a: Further, from those things which have so far been set out in these and the preceding theses, it is manifest that there is no controversy here, Whether the Blessed, both men and Angels, are worthy of some worship and honor, and are to be treated so by us: for this the Doctors of the Reformed School freely confess and teach, nor can the contrary be imputed to them except through calumny.
pass_b: From what these theses and the earlier ones have set out so far, it is clear that there is no dispute here over whether the blessed, both men and angels, deserve some kind of reverence and honor and ought to receive it from us. The teachers of the Reformed school readily admit and teach this, and the contrary cannot be laid to their charge except by slander.

choices.why: Here cultus is the broad honor both sides grant, not religious worship; 'reverence' avoids implying latria.

sections.title: Both sides agree the honor of saints is not of one species with divine worship
sections.pass_a: Moreover it is evident from this that the Doctors of the Roman School, with the Reformed, acknowledge that the worship which is owed to holy men and Angels is not contained under the same univocal genus with divine worship; and therefore is not of the same species with it: nor is that worship Religious, properly and strictly speaking: but only in a certain broader and less proper signification: according to which notable Theologians among the Reformed expressly admit that the worship owed to the Saints can be called religious.
pass_b: It is also clear from this that the teachers of the Roman school agree with the Reformed that the honor owed to holy men and angels does not fall under one univocal genus with divine worship, and so is not of the same species. Nor is that honor religious in the proper and strict sense, but only in a broader and less proper sense. In that sense, eminent theologians among the Reformed expressly allow that the honor owed to the saints may be called religious.

lemmas.gloss: in a broader and less proper signification

choices.why: A scholastic term of art; keeping 'univocal' preserves the precise logical claim.

sections.title: Latria and dulia: a school distinction both sides can tolerate
sections.pass_a: This too has been shown by us, that the Doctors of the Roman School confess that the distinction of Religious worship into Latria and Dulia is an invention of the School; nor is the difference of those words, as they are used in the Roman School, exactly kept in Scripture: for Dulia is more often restricted to the worship proper to God, but Latria sometimes extended to human service. In turn, however, the Doctors of the Reformed School do not much resist that, for the sake of distinction, Latria be fitted to divine worship, but Dulia to that observance by which creatures can and ought to be honored.
pass_b: We have also shown that the teachers of the Roman school admit that the division of religious worship into latria and dulia is an invention of the schools, and that Scripture does not strictly keep the difference between these words as the Roman school uses them. Dulia is more often confined there to the worship proper to God, while latria is sometimes extended to service rendered to human beings.

The teachers of the Reformed school, for their part, do not much object if, for clarity's sake, latria is assigned to divine worship and dulia to the respect with which creatures may and should be honored.

choices.why: Technical terms kept as is; the thesis is about the words themselves.

sections.title: The real question: shrines, rites, oaths, vows, relative honor, and prayer addressed to saints
sections.pass_a: The whole difficulty and question therefore returns to this, In what thing consists the honor which can lawfully be shown to holy and blessed creatures, and especially to the most Blessed Virgin Mary? Namely, whether sacred buildings can not only be called by the name of Saints and Angels, for the sake of distinction, but also be founded for this end, that in them Angels and holy men already received into heaven be publicly invoked, and honored with various rites; before them as if looking at us, by bending the knees, and bowing the body, by burning incense to them, by lighting candles, and by offering various gifts? Whether it is lawful to swear by them, and to make vows to them relatively to God, that is, insofar as the truth of God shines out in them, and God dwells in them through glory? And finally, Whether we can ask them to pray for us: and this not simply, but to direct prayers to them, in another sense indeed, but conceived in the same words and formulas as are those which we conceive to God? Which the Doctors of the Roman School affirm and the Roman Church confirms by its practice, but the Protestants by common consent deny.
pass_b: The whole difficulty and question therefore comes down to this: what does the honor consist in that may lawfully be given to holy and blessed creatures, and above all to the most Blessed Virgin Mary?

May churches not only be named after saints and angels to tell them apart, but also be built for the purpose of publicly invoking in them the angels and holy men already received into heaven, and of honoring them with various rites: kneeling and bowing before them as though they were watching us, burning incense to them, lighting candles, and offering all kinds of gifts?

May one swear by them and make vows to them relatively to God, that is, insofar as God's truth shines in them and God dwells in them through glory? And finally, may we ask them to pray for us, and not simply ask, but address prayers to them, meant in a different sense, to be sure, yet framed in the same words and formulas as those we address to God?
The teachers of the Roman school affirm all this, and the Roman Church confirms it by its practice; the Protestants with one voice deny it.

lemmas.gloss: as if they were looking at us

choices.why: Sacred buildings in context are churches and chapels; 'churches' reads naturally.

sections.title: Saints as guardians and mediators, and Mary as Queen of Heaven, rejected by Protestants
sections.pass_a: Moreover this is in controversy, Whether it is lawful to celebrate the Saints who died in Christ as guardians and patrons of the human race, to whom the government of our affairs has been committed by God: And to hold them as such Mediators and Intercessors with God, who at every time can hear and perceive the prayers of all men conceived either in heart or in mouth, and offer and commend them to God, and help with their suffrages and merits? But especially, Whether the Blessed Virgin is to be acknowledged and proclaimed as Queen of heaven, and of the whole world, and Lady of all creatures: as she through whom the world has been saved, and who alone has slain all heresies: And whether she ought to be saluted Mother of mercy, Mother and fount of grace, our life and hope: all of which the practice of the Roman Church approves. But the Protestants disapprove and condemn them.
pass_b: A further point in dispute is whether it is lawful to celebrate the saints who have died in Christ as guardians and patrons of the human race, entrusted by God with the government of our affairs, and to treat them as mediators and intercessors with God who can at all times hear and take in the prayers of all people, whether spoken in the heart or with the lips, offer and commend them to God, and help with their own suffrages and merits.

Above all, the question is whether the Blessed Virgin should be acknowledged and proclaimed Queen of Heaven and of the whole world and Lady of all creatures, as the one through whom the world was saved and who alone has destroyed all heresies, and whether she should be hailed as Mother of mercy, Mother and fountain of grace, our life and our hope. The practice of the Roman Church approves all of this; the Protestants reject and condemn it.

lemmas.gloss: who alone has slain all heresies

choices.why: The fixed liturgical title is kept as a title.

sections.title: Further scandalous titles: goddess, tutelary deities, Mary's dominion over her Son
sections.pass_a: To them also very many other Eulogies give scandal, which are heaped upon the Blessed Virgin and the Saints, by private Doctors indeed; but the Roman Church not disapproving, nor forbidding: As that the title of Goddess is attributed to the Virgin Mary, that the Saints are called Tutelary Deities: as in that inscription which I remember having read a few years ago, in the Church at Troyes dedicated to Blessed Peter, Peter, Helen, Mastidia, Tutelary deities of the people of Troyes. And that to the Virgin Mary is attributed command and Dominion over the son himself, and the power of dispensing under God all gifts of Grace and nature, and of communicating them to whom she wills. That she is called the enlightener of hearts, and the cause of things: indeed she is said to have founded and made the world, and to preserve and govern all things which are in it: and more of this kind, which for brevity's sake we omit for the present.
pass_b: The Protestants are also offended by many other tributes heaped on the Blessed Virgin and the saints. These come from private teachers, it is true, but the Roman Church neither disapproves nor forbids them.

So the Virgin Mary is given the title of goddess, and the saints are called tutelary deities, as in an inscription I remember reading a few years ago in the church at Troyes dedicated to Saint Peter: "Peter, Helen, Mastidia, tutelary deities of Troyes."

The Virgin Mary is credited with command and dominion over her own Son and with power to dispense under God all the gifts of grace and nature and to share them with whomever she wills. She is called the enlightener of hearts and the cause of things; she is even said to have founded and made the world and to preserve and govern all that is in it. There is more of this kind, which we pass over for now for brevity's sake.

lemmas.gloss: command and dominion over the son himself
